hints.title: Oracle Guidance Obstacle
hints.text: The query function informs you whether your pick is higher (-1), lower (1), or exact (0). What midpoint strategy guarantees finding the target in at most 31 queries for numbers up to 2^31 - 1?

hints.title: Bisection Feedback Invariant
hints.text: If guess(mid) == -1, the picked number is strictly smaller than mid (right = mid - 1). If guess(mid) == 1, pick is strictly larger (left = mid + 1).

hints.title: Midpoint Query Procedure
hints.text: Initialize left = 1 and right = n. While left <= right, compute mid = left + (right - left) // 2. Call res = guess(mid). If res == 0, return mid. If res == -1, set right = mid - 1; otherwise set left = mid + 1.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

complexity.notes: Logarithmic bisection halving search space per API call in O(1) space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Linear guessing requires up to 2 * 10^9 queries which exceeds runtime limits.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Avoiding 32-bit signed integer overflow when computing mid = left + (right - left) // 2.

solutions.approach: Bisection driven by guess API response
